newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices mostly hold, bears wait.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices mostly hold, bears wait.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices, helped by stable crude, mostly held steady Wednesday in thin trade, but sentiment remained mostly bearish amid cheap natgas and milder weather forecasts, sources said.

"The weather is terrible and oil prices are still too high relative to gas. It feels weak," said one cash trader, adding a number of East Coast utilities recently have made the switch to cheaper natural gas.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent remained talked in the $16.25-50 a barrel area, with March one percent paper also quoted little changed at about $16, traders said.
A prompt, 75,000-barrel NYH one percent deal in the $16.35 area could not be confirmed.
NYH April one percent paper was pegged at $15.60-85, steady to down slightly from Tuesday.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour and high pour notionally held steady at $19.25 and $17.25-50, respectively.
NYH high sulphurs were unchanged to down slightly, with 2.2 percent now straddling $15, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with one percent still at $14.75-15.00 and three percent at $12.75 or lower.

March New York city gate gas prices also held steady Wednesday at about the $2.10-15/mmBtu level, or about $13.42 a barrel equivalent. March gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed slightly to about $1.80/mmBtu, or $11.34 a barrel equivalent.
